clue.text: He is behind the man taking delivery

definitions.text: He is behind the man taking delivery

parts.words: He is behind the man taking delivery
parts.note: in cricket the batsman receives each ball bowled, and the gloved fielder crouches just behind him to catch what he misses

explanation.surface: Someone stands behind a man receiving a parcel or a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a parcel or childbirth, but in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; the 'man taking delivery' is the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket fielder stationed directly behind the batsman's stumps to catch or stop balls he misses.

clue.text: Look out, timekeeper has the very thing

parts.note: a wristwatch keeps time
'it' means the ideal, the very thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A warning shout that a clock or watch is exactly what is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are colloquial warnings telling someone to be careful.

clue.text: French cry odds in manner that's lively, brisk and decisive

parts.note: cri is the French word for a cry or shout
SP, starting price, is the betting odds on a racehorse when the race begins

explanation.surface: A French exclamation and some betting odds, delivered in a sharp, energetic way.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is the bookmakers' odds at the off in British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a manner of speech or action that is quick, sharp and to the point.

clue.text: Running off to the match

parts.note: a match here is a marriage, so dashing away to wed in secret, rather than racing to a football game

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying away to watch a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a game, but it is a marriage: running away to get married.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretly leaving home to marry, typically without parental consent.

clue.text: Bird had equipment before start of expedition

indicators.note: one piece comes ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment

indicators.note: the first letter of the word expedition is taken

explanation.surface: A bird had its gear packed before setting off on an expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey of the hawk family, with a forked tail.

clue.text: How traveller perhaps investigated thoroughly

definitions.meaning: describing how a traveller went about new lands: roaming and discovering them
examined in detail, looked into fully

explanation.surface: An account of how a traveller went about examining something carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller roams unknown places; to investigate a subject thoroughly is to probe every corner of it.

clue.text: Lady, one going before beth

definitions.meaning: the name that comes ahead of the letters beth to form a longer royal woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman who comes before the Hebrew letter beth in the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beth' suggests the Hebrew alphabet, where aleph precedes it; instead it is the end of Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, the opening part of Elizabeth, as with Eliza Doolittle.

clue.text: Sacked!

parts.note: read literally as put into a sack, and also the idiom for something already secured and certain

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone has lost their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' looks like dismissal from work; read literally it is placed in a sack, which is also a phrase for a sure thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning certain to succeed or already secured, as well as literally inside a sack.

clue.text: Muse about princess in Ukraine

indicators.note: the princess's letters are placed within those for the country

parts.note: UA is the international code for Ukraine
a rani is an Indian queen or princess

explanation.surface: A muse about a royal princess living in Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is only a link here; the insertion is signalled by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the patron of astronomy.

clue.text: Balding slim leg-spinner

parts.note: thin means slim
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: A bald, skinny bowler who spins the ball from leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg-spinner' reads as one cricket bowler, but it splits into two pieces; the on side is the cricket name for the leg side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing hair on the crown of the head, a euphemism for going bald.

clue.text: This man is on target

parts.note: on an archery or darts target, the ring just around the bullseye, and a shot landing there

explanation.surface: A man described as accurate or on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' suggests a person, but the clue means a shot or ring on a target, close to the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery and shooting, the ring next to the bullseye, or a shot that hits it.

clue.text: Flea found in the fields in Kent

definitions.meaning: a flea is an insect that jumps

definitions.text: found in the fields in Kent
definitions.meaning: a person who picks hops in the hop fields of Kent, the English county famed for them

explanation.surface: A flea discovered in Kentish farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, traditionally full of hop gardens where Londoners went hop-picking.
explanation.definitionFit: Any jumping insect, and also a hop-picker working the Kentish harvest.

clue.text: Joan embraced husband Nathaniel first or another man

indicators.note: the woman's name wraps round the other letters as if hugging them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Nat comes before the husband's letter

parts.note: Nat is the short form of Nathaniel

explanation.surface: Joan hugged her husband, with Nathaniel first in line, or some other man.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, so simply a different man from those named.

clue.text: Posh wooden objects going round dish

indicators.note: the wooden objects surround the posh letter

parts.note: treen is small domestic items made of wood
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Smart wooden ornaments being passed round a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' classification of English usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep covered serving bowl for soup.

clue.text: Force into transport merger

parts.note: two kinds of transport joined together: trains and motor traffic
two kinds of transport joined together: trains and motor traffic

explanation.surface: Pressure to push through a merger of transport firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force into' is the definition: to railroad someone is to push them into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To pressure someone hastily into an action, or to push a measure through without debate.

clue.text: Green item of clothing found going round oriental joint

indicators.note: the two outer pieces sit either side of the eastern letter

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry
a bra is an undergarment
E for eastern

explanation.surface: A green garment wrapped around an Eastern joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Vert is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the bones of the spine, which articulate as joints.

clue.text: Oddly Tim's about to make mistake with alternative for violence

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the other pieces
the letters of Tim's are arranged in an odd, unusual way

parts.note: the letters T I M S
to err is to make a mistake
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Tim strangely errs, taking another course towards violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but here it signals a rearrangement, and 'about' wraps the scrambled name around the mistake and the alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: The use of violence and intimidation for political ends.

clue.text: Liqueur mixed in tea-set!

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A liqueur blended inside a tea service.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured sweet liqueur.

clue.text: Person from UK, Troy, takes some to part of France

parts.note: a Brit is a British person
t is the abbreviation for troy, the weight system
any means some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A British man called Troy taking a group to a region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy' looks like a man's name, but it is the troy weight system, abbreviated t.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of north-west France, a peninsula with Celtic heritage.

clue.text: Saw how badly he bled

indicators.note: the letters are put together poorly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A witness describing how badly a man was bleeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of behold, to see or observe.

clue.text: Mention something unpleasant from boring person at university

parts.note: a drag is a tedious person or thing
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A dull student at college bringing up awkward subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a painful or embarrassing matter from the past.

clue.text: Promise, before time, to produce wad

indicators.note: the promise comes ahead of the time letter

parts.note: a pledge is a promise

explanation.surface: A vow made in good time to produce a bundle of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wad' suggests money, but here it is a small pad of lint for a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pad of cotton or lint used to dress a wound.

clue.text: Not soft currency?

parts.note: soft currency is one that is weak on the exchange markets; its opposite in firmness is ready money in notes and coins

explanation.surface: A question about whether some money is a strong currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard is the opposite of soft, and cash is currency; the phrase means ready money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money in coins and notes rather than cheques or credit.

clue.text: Provide what is required but react badly

indicators.note: the letters of react are put together in a jumbled way

explanation.surface: Supply what is needed but then respond poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply food or services meeting someone's needs.

clue.text: Force in alternator questioned

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the phrase alternator questioned

explanation.surface: Doubts raised about the power in a car's alternator.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisting or rotational force, as in an engine.

clue.text: Heard singers have number of sheets

indicators.note: the word for the singers is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers

explanation.surface: Singers heard to possess a number of sheets of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper.

clue.text: Menacing appearance of sailor leaving work

indicators.note: the sailor departs, so his letters are removed

parts.note: labour is work
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A threatening look from a seaman quitting his job.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowl or threatening look, from the verb to frown darkly.

clue.text: Smallest number taking field way

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A small group taking a path across a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum, the smallest amount or quantity possible.

clue.text: Regulating pair first who are being unfaithful

indicators.note: the pair is placed ahead of the regulating word

parts.note: a pair is two
timing is setting or regulating, as with an engine

explanation.surface: Setting a couple first among those who cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceiving one partner by seeing another at the same time.

clue.text: Without any outstanding commitments

parts.note: owing nothing to anyone, with all loans and bills settled

explanation.surface: Someone with nothing left to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing no money to creditors, having paid all one owes.
